verses.text: Now about food offered to idols: “We all have knowledge,” you say. But knowledge can puff up your ego; love builds people up.
If someone thinks they know it all, they still haven’t learned what they need to know.
But whoever loves God is known by God.
So, about eating food offered to idols: we know an idol has no real existence, and there is no God except the one.
People call plenty of things “gods”—in heaven or on earth. Folks talk about many “gods” and many “lords,”
but for us there is one God, the Father, from whom everything comes and for whom we live; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom everything came and through whom we live.
Not everyone has that understanding. Some people are still used to idols; when they eat that food, they think they’re eating something offered to an idol, and their tender conscience gets stained.
Food doesn’t bring us closer to God. We’re no worse if we don’t eat, and no better if we do.
So watch your step: don’t let your freedom become a tripwire for someone whose faith is still growing.
If someone with a tender conscience sees you—someone who “knows better”—eating in an idol’s temple, won’t they get pushed to eat food offered to idols too?
Then your knowledge can wreck a believer whose faith is weak—the very brother or sister Christ died for.
When you sin against fellow believers like that and wound their tender conscience, you’re sinning against Christ.
So if eating meat makes my brother or sister stumble, I won’t eat meat again. I refuse to be the reason they fall.
